extracted.intended_audience: university/college faculty and administrators developing or implementing peer teaching assessment programs (example: schools of pharmacy)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and validating a faculty-driven peer observation and evaluation program (for large classroom teaching) including a structured instrument (POET), training, logistics, and procedures for formative feedback. Focus is on creating a reliable, feasible, and transferable peer-assessment system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a clear vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a collaborative statement of purpose for the peer assessment program (example provided: 'to promote the improvement of teaching and learning') and align the program with a departmental teaching philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The departmental teaching philosophy elements should serve as the blueprint for the peer assessment program; consensus among faculty on vision is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate between formative and summative review
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the peer review system will be formative, summative, or a combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Taskforce chose a formative system to provide feedback for professional growth and development; formative processes emphasize improvement over judgment and affect decisions about announcement of visits, use of results, and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify program leader and coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate strong leadership (e.g., co-chairs) during development and a coordinator for implementation and monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership should achieve consensus, attain faculty buy-in, and integrate peer assessment into departmental culture; a coordinator is likely necessary for logistics and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify participants and peer observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Define who will be assessed and who may serve as peer observers, and set policies on mandatory participation and observer qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the study, participation as observed faculty was mandatory for all department faculty; serving as an observer was voluntary but required completion of formal training. Faculty could decline one evaluator pairing; pairing should be managed by the program coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a process (pre-observation, observation, post-observation, post-assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a staged process with pre-observation meeting, a teaching observation record during class, post-observation meeting, and a post-assessment meeting tied to student assessment results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-meeting: review materials and context; Observation: use 'plus' and 'delta' columns to record positives and areas for improvement and identify 2–3 main focus areas; Post-observation meeting: intensive self-reflection and discussion; Post-assessment meeting: review exam questions/item analysis to evaluate student mastery. Timing of each meeting and participant responsibilities are specified in Appendix 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify or develop a peer evaluation instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Select or construct a valid and reliable instrument tailored to the teaching context (large classroom) to standardize observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing instruments lacked validation for this context, so the Taskforce developed POET by mapping educational philosophy components to items from a master list, piloting, ranking items, and removing low-importance items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate observer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide formal training for peer observers to increase acceptance, standardize what to observe and how to give feedback, and to support reliability of the instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taskforce conducted a 4-hour training session including use of the teaching observation record, role play, and practice with prerecorded lectures. Only those completing formal training may serve as observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide logistics (observer count, announced vs unannounced visits, observation length, selection of lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear policy decisions about how observations will be scheduled and conducted to balance feasibility with fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions included: ordinarily one observer once tool proven reliable (multiple observers allowed if summative), announced/scheduled visits (pre-observation meeting valued → announced), optimal observation is entire lecture though half may be acceptable, each instructor observed at least once per year, instructors choose the lecture to be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish time commitment, incentives, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the total time required and specify incentives or consequences to promote participation and sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated total time commitment per observation (including all meetings and paperwork) was 4–8 hours. Observers received service credit; participation as observed faculty was mandatory and documented in merit evaluations; because the process was formative, results were not included in merit reports—only documentation of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish communication modes and record-keeping/reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Create written policies describing process, expectations, and maintain program records; determine how feedback is communicated to the instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written 'rules of the game' document, program coordinator tracks matches and participation, observers provide a written letter summarizing outcomes (formative, given only to the instructor), and letters may be included in promotion/merit dossiers at instructor's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an educational expert and faculty-derived philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlist educational expertise during development and ground the instrument in the department's educational philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An educational expert advised development and training; mapping the department's teaching philosophy to instrument items served as the blueprint for item selection and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate self-reflection and personal interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed reflection-on-action and structured faculty self-reflection into pre-observation, post-observation, and post-assessment meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection prompts should examine choices, outcomes, strengths, areas for improvement, and potential strategies; the most intensive reflection occurs at the post-observation meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'checklist' mentality during live observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers should not complete the formal instrument during the lecture; instead use an observation record to capture concrete notes and complete the instrument afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The educational expert recommended using a teaching observation record during class (plus/delta columns) and completing the POET after the lecture to prevent checklist behavior and allow attention to classroom dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative-purpose confidentiality and use of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Use peer assessment primarily as formative feedback for improvement; keep detailed feedback between observer and instructor unless instructor chooses to include it elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written letters summarizing outcomes are provided to the instructor for formative purposes only; this approach helps alleviate fears around privacy and punitive misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum frequency of observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how often faculty should be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Taskforce agreed each instructor should be observed at least once per year; instructors encouraged to rotate lectures and target lectures with perceived problems or poor student evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observer selection and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Program coordinator should match faculty with trained observers based on scheduling and availability; faculty may decline a pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content expertise of the observer is not required generally but may be desirable in some circumstances and should be discussed ahead of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement policy for observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether observations are announced or unannounced based on program goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because pre-observation meeting and formative aims were valued, the Taskforce chose announced, scheduled visits to allow context-setting and to reduce anxiety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation duration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Define whether full-lecture observation is required or partial observation acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entire lecture observation is optimal; for longer lectures, observing half is acceptable but observer should attempt to assess instructor-student interaction before or after class as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching observation record format (+/Δ columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a simple two-column teaching observation record: a 'plus' column for positive aspects and a 'delta' column for potential improvements, best practices not observed, or questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers record during lecture, then review to identify 2–3 most significant positive and negative themes to inform the POET completion and feedback letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of POET (sections and item counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: POET consists of 39 ranked items organized into: pre-observation visit (8 items + scripted interview questions), classroom observation—content (5 items), teaching strategies and presentation skills (17 items), classroom climate (5 items), post-observation meeting (rubric for reflection, no ranked items), and post-assessment meeting (4 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The classroom observation component (27 items) was the focus of interrater reliability testing; pre- and post- sections include guided open-ended dialogue questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item response scale (rating categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranked items use a forced-choice scale: accomplished well (AW), accomplished (A), needs development (ND), needs significant development (NSD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To force a commitment, neutral/undecided/not applicable options are not included. For certain items that might not be observable, a 'did not observe (DNO)' option was added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Did Not Observe' (DNO) option
rubrics_metrics.description: For items unlikely to be routinely observed, include a DNO response to avoid forcing inaccurate ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taskforce identified 4 classroom items for which observers might reasonably select DNO; analysis of DNO responses informed later item revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item selection and content validity process
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop item pool from literature and local philosophy, pilot items, have taskforce rank items, remove items with low importance, and revise descriptors for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial draft had 123 items; items scoring <3 (on 1–5 scale) were removed, remaining items clarified and reorganized; external national experts were solicited to rank items and provide feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing and interrater reliability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot the instrument with trained observers and compute interrater reliability (ICC) for the classroom observation component using appropriate statistical models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eight lectures with 2–3 observers were tested; two-way random effects, consistency-type ICCs were used; ICCs ranged from 0.66 to 0.97 (average measures), supporting good interrater reliability for this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: External review and minor revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain external expert review of items and revise item descriptors and rubric based on feedback to improve clarity and content validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three nationally recognized reviewers ranked all items ≥3 and suggested clarifications and added descriptors; minor changes were made post-pilot without re-evaluating reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and written feedback letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers provide a final written letter summarizing strengths and the 2–3 main focus areas (post-assessment meeting) for the instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter is formative, provided to the instructor, and may be included in promotion/merit documents at the instructor's option; the observer should complete Section 4 of the POET prior to the post-assessment meeting and limit final recommendations to 2–3 items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe expectations for meetings and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Set timelines for pre-observation, post-observation, and post-assessment meetings and for materials submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-observation meeting: ~1 week before observation; faculty should provide lecture materials at least 1 week prior. Post-observation meeting: within 1–2 weeks. Post-assessment meeting: within 2 weeks of the first major examination following the observation; faculty should submit original exam questions and item analysis prior to the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate of overall time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a realistic estimate of time required for one peer observation activity including training, observation, meetings, paperwork, and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on literature and field tests, estimate 4–8 hours total per peer observation (including pre/post meetings and documentation). Communicate this estimate clearly to faculty to increase buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing faculty concerns and barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and plan to mitigate barriers such as fears about privacy, judgmental culture, workload, bias, and lack of buy-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barriers can be addressed with a valid and reliable instrument, formative orientation, transparent policies, training on constructive feedback, and possible incentives; strong faculty involvement in development promotes acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies on inclusion of peer assessment in merit/promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how peer assessment documentation is recorded and whether content will be included in merit, promotion, or tenure dossiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this program, participation was documented for merit reviews but formative results were not included; letters may be included by the faculty member at their discretion; summative observations can be arranged if faculty request them for promotion/tenure support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation regarding content expertise of observer
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether observer content expertise is necessary when pairing observers and instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot results suggested lack of content expertise did not impede peer assessment of delivery, strategies, and climate; however, content expertise may be desirable in some cases and should be discussed prior to observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of program coordinator for logistics and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a coordinator to match observers, track participation, maintain records, and oversee program logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator responsibilities include scheduling, record-keeping, and ensuring faculty complete training; central coordination helps sustain the program and training cycles.
